newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower as soybean futures collapse.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower as soybean futures collapse.

text.p: Spillover selling from a collapse in the soybean pit pressured CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
Corn traded firm most of the session, supported by USDA's cut in corn ending stocks for the 1996-97 marketing year, they said.
USDA Friday said the supply of corn in the U.S. on August 31 would total 909 million bushels, below the previous outlook for 959 million bushels.
"The report tells us they overestimated the corn and bean crops last year," a trader said.
Corn also was underpinned by weather uncertainties.
Cold, wet weather in the upper Midwest led to concerns about delays in the seeding of the U.S. corn crop, sources said.

Traders said funds sold roughly 10 million bushels of corn. Griffin Trading sold five million bushels of May, Cargill Inc sold three million May and Rosenthal Collins sold two million bushels of May, traders said.
Corn futures closed one to 4-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with May down 4-1/4 at $2.99-1/2 a bushel. July was down four cents at $3.01-1/2.

In spread trading, Prudential Securities did seven million bushels of July/May at one to 1-1/4 cents, premium July, traders said. O'Connor and Co did three million May/July at one to 1-1/4 cents, premium July and Dean Witter spread two million bushels of July/May at two cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts, above Thursday's volume of 64,308 contracts.

In corn options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 1,500 May $3.00 calls at 6-1/2 to 8-1/2 cents, Lind Waldock bought 1,100 July $3.10 calls at 13 to 13-1/2 cents and Refco Inc bought 600 May $3.10 calls at four cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, slightly above the 19,188 traded Thursday.
